plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 (20-layer periodic Bragg cold mirror) based on prior iteration results. Best candidate achieved 0.8497 target score with 9 valid candidates. Three refinement routes proposed: (1) Local exploitation around Candidate 0's thickness profile with narrow Gaussian reinitialization and reduced optimizer step-size per feedback directives; (2) Expand to 25 layers while preserving HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology to test if additional layers improve stopband reflectance; (3) Expand to maximum 30 layers with quarter-wave initialization to explore the full manufacturing budget. All routes maintain parent_route_id = route_01 as required by refinement chain.

routes.execution_request_english: Perform one bounded TMM thickness optimization for an exactly 20-layer planar stack. Use the fixed material sequence from the incident side: HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica / HfO2 / Fused Silica. Optimize only the physical thickness of each finite layer within the user-declared bounds. Do not optimize material identity or layer count in this route. Optimize a 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 alternating stack on fused silica substrate at normal incidence. Initialize thicknesses from the following baseline profile (in nm, starting from air side): [53.0, 272.0, 81.0, 83.0, 55.0, 94.0, 94.0, 91.0, 245.0, 92.0, 68.0, 196.0, 54.0, 84.0, 77.0, 211.0, 162.0, 74.0, 135.0, 86.0]. Apply Gaussian perturbation with standard deviation σ = 8 nm for population reinitialization. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with step-size multiplier reduced by 50% relative to default to prioritize local exploitation. Evaluate at wavelengths 1530-1565 nm (transmittance objective) and 400-700 nm (reflectance objective). Total layer count fixed at 20. Material sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2... (odd layers HfO2, even layers SiO2). Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 30.
routes.revision_reason: Per feedback directives: reinitialize evolutionary population from Candidate 0's Round 1 thickness profile using narrow Gaussian (σ = 8 nm) and reduce optimizer step-size multiplier by 50% to prioritize local exploitation over global exploration, capitalizing on the verified feasible region.

routes.title: 25-Layer Extended Bragg Stack with Quarter-Wave Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 20 to 25 while maintaining HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology will improve visible band reflectance (400-700 nm) due to increased stopband depth, with minimal degradation to telecom band transmittance (1530-1565 nm) if thicknesses are properly optimized.
routes.design_principle: Extend the verified 20-layer Bragg mirror topology by 5 additional layer pairs to increase stopband reflectance while using quarter-wave thickness initialization at a reference wavelength balanced between the two operational bands.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 8 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (16 finite layers)
design_variables: All 25 layer thicknesses, initialized from quarter-wave condition at 900 nm reference wavelength
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maintain total layer count at exactly 25
manufacturing_considerations: Additional 5 layers increase deposition time and potential thickness accumulation error
theory_basis: Bragg mirror stopband depth increases with layer pair count
Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance coatings
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer calculation
expected_advantages: Higher visible band reflectance due to increased layer count
Maintained telecom transmittance if optimization balances both bands
Tests whether 20 layers was limiting performance or near-optimal
known_risks: Additional layers may increase absorption losses in visible band
May not improve target score if 20 layers already sufficient for required reflectance
Increased complexity may reduce optimizer convergence reliability

routes.revision_reason: Explores whether increasing layer count from 20 to 25 improves performance while maintaining the same HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology verified in route_01. Tests if the 20-layer configuration was performance-limited by layer count.

routes.scientific_hypothesis: Using the full 30-layer manufacturing budget with HfO2/SiO2 alternating topology will maximize visible band reflectance while maintaining telecom transmittance, representing the theoretical performance ceiling for this material system under the given constraints.
routes.design_principle: Maximize layer count to 30 (the manufacturing limit) to achieve maximum stopband depth in the visible band, with quarter-wave initialization at a reference wavelength optimized for dual-band performance.

research_influence: Evidence ID s2-chunk:CorpusId:92993850:s2chunk:92993850:1765:3736:69b2ad685bc8c493 confirms telecom C-band (1550 nm) importance for satellite quantum communication, motivating the high-priority focus on 1530-1565 nm transmittance in all routes.

Prior iteration results (best_target_score = 0.8497, 9 valid candidates) directly informed the local exploitation strategy in route_01_refine_local, using Candidate 0's thickness profile as the initialization baseline.
Feedback directives explicitly required narrow Gaussian reinitialization (σ = 8 nm) and 50% step-size reduction, which are incorporated into route_01_refine_local execution request.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 20, 25, or 30 layers provides optimal performance-to-complexity ratio cannot be determined until all three refinement routes complete.
The optimal reference wavelength for quarter-wave initialization (850 nm vs 900 nm vs other values) remains an open optimization variable.
Incidence angle was not specified in original request; all routes assume normal incidence but angled incidence may be relevant for satellite applications.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
